# Cost screen — what the owned data says about tradeable cost

**EXPLORATORY SCREENING — NO VERDICTS.** Generated by `tools/cost_screen.py` on the archives and archived results as of 2026-09-22. Bounds and arithmetic only; no claim about the market is tested here, and nothing in this document may be cited as a verdict. Interpretation follows the generated tables.

## S1 — the tick floor (a hard lower bound on round-trip cost)

One cent is the minimum price increment for names ≥ $1.00. Crossing the spread costs at least one tick on entry **and** one on exit, so `2 × tick` is the narrowest conceivable round trip — before any real spread, slippage, impact or locate fee.

**mover (roster names)** — 400 name-days, 307 names, median price $7.78

| price band | name-days | median $ | 1 tick | round trip (2 ticks) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | 47 | 1.47 | 0.680% | **1.361%** |
| 2-5 | 94 | 3.29 | 0.304% | **0.609%** |
| 5-10 | 103 | 7.29 | 0.137% | **0.274%** |
| 10-20 | 156 | 14.16 | 0.071% | **0.141%** |

**index (S&P 600 window)** — 1,805 name-days, 601 names, median price $42.54

| price band | name-days | median $ | 1 tick | round trip (2 ticks) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2-5 | 28 | 4.06 | 0.246% | **0.493%** |
| 5-10 | 98 | 7.45 | 0.134% | **0.268%** |
| 10-20 | 230 | 14.73 | 0.068% | **0.136%** |
| >20 | 1,449 | 52.14 | 0.019% | **0.038%** |

For reference, the frozen cost convention in every intraday engine is **0.15% round trip**.

## S2 — break-even cost for the archived families

`mean_ret` in the archived results is the **net** absolute mean (after the frozen 0.15%). Gross = net + 0.15%, and gross is exactly the round-trip cost at which the family breaks even. A negative gross means no cost assumption can help — the leg loses before costs.

| campaign / leg | n | net mean | implied gross | break-even cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #15 B-01 long (index) | 1,963 | -0.2068% | **-0.0568%** | -0.0568% |
| #19 reversal long (index) | 43,722 | -0.1991% | **-0.0491%** | -0.0491% |
| #19 reversal short (index) | 41,985 | -0.1073% | **+0.0427%** | +0.0427% |

The contrasts (#15 F2 reach-rate, #19 F2/F3, #21 veto slots, #22 F2, #27 gate slots) are *differences* between legs and carry no absolute level, so no tradeable break-even can be read off them — a contrast says which of two things is worse, not whether either makes money.

## S3 — how much room exists per minute and per holding window

A trade can only pay if price moves more than the round trip costs. These are the distributions of the *available* relative range — per minute, and over the engines' N=60-bar horizon — so the share below a given cost tier is the share of moments that are untradeable by construction.

**index (S&P 600, window ≥ 2026-08-19)** — 18,071 files, 5,021,093 minutes

## S4 — foresight bounds on the frozen event sets

Three columns, all **gross** (before cost), all on the exact frozen event sets:

- **as measured** — the repo's convention (`O[e+1] → C[e+N]`);
- **best exit** — realistic entry, but the *best close inside the holding window* (foresight on the exit only);
- **perfect foresight** — buy the window's lowest low, sell its highest high (short: sell the high, cover the low). No execution achieves this; it is a hard **upper bound** on what any fill model could deliver.

If the perfect-foresight column cannot clear the tick floor, the hypothesis is unreachable — no quotes feed, no execution skill and no parameter change can rescue it.

### #15 B-01 micro pullback (index, frozen detector — long-only set)

| direction | n | as measured | best exit / cover | perfect foresight |

| long (the claim) | 2,401 | -0.0407% | +0.6447% | +1.4660% |
| short (its mirror) | 2,401 | +0.0407% | — | +1.4347% |

Tick floor on this population: median **0.060%** round trip (p10 0.021%, p90 0.238%).

**Unreachable trades** — the share of signals whose perfect-foresight gross is below the cost tier. For these the trade cannot pay however well it is executed: the window simply does not contain enough range.

## Interpretation

*(hand-written from the tables above; a re-run regenerates the tables and
preserves this section, so any changed number must be re-read into it.)*

### 1. The two long legs lose money before any cost is charged

Gross (before cost) absolute means on the frozen event sets: **−0.041%** for
#15's B-01 long, **−0.044%** for #19's reversal-long events (−0.057% for the
archived #15 family, which pairs against baselines). A negative gross cannot be
rescued by *any* cost assumption, fill model or execution skill — the entry leg
is already losing when the round trip is free. The archived FADE verdicts are
therefore **conservative**: the legs are worse than "fades", and no quotes feed
is needed to establish that.

### 2. The only positive intraday legs earn less than the minimum crossing

The positive absolute legs in the whole intraday record are the *shorts*:
#19's short-direction events at **+0.040%** gross, and the mirror of the
long-direction events at **+0.044%**. The median **tick floor** on those very
events is **0.062%** round trip (p10 0.020%). So the best absolute intraday
edge the project has ever measured is **smaller than the cost of crossing the
spread twice at one cent a side** — the cheapest possible round trip on those
names. Only in the cheapest-to-cross decile (floor ≈ 2bp) does a ~2bp margin
exist, before real spreads, slippage, fees and short-locate costs.

This is the cleanest cost-based kill in the screen, and it is arithmetic rather
than a verdict: the fade direction was never the claim anyway, and its measured
magnitude sits inside the noise of the tick.

### 3. The cost convention is sound for the index and unsound for the movers

- **Index population** (601 names, median $42.54): 80% of name-days sit above
  $20, where the 2-tick floor is **0.038%**. Only ~7% of name-days have a floor
  above the frozen **0.15%**. The archived index verdicts therefore do **not**
  depend on a generous cost assumption — they would survive a cost model four
  times *cheaper* than the one used.
- **Mover population** (307 names, median $7.78): the 2-tick floor is
  **0.274%** in the $5–10 band, **0.609%** in $2–5, **1.361%** in $1–2, and
  **61% of roster name-days have a floor above 0.15%**. Against the movers'
  median 60-bar window range of 1.465%, the tick floor alone consumes **19%**
  ($5–10), **42%** ($2–5) and **93%** ($1–2) of the available move — with the
  real spread on top of the floor, by definition.

**Consequence for pre-reg #33:** inheriting `COST = 0.15%` would flatter its
results by 2–9× on most of its population. The freeze must settle the cost
model (recorded in PREREGISTRATION #33 §5) — either keep 0.15% as a
comparability tier and add a tick-floor-aware sensitivity, or set the primary
cost from a measured spread sample once quotes exist.

### 4. On the index, the constraint is the signal, not the room

The median 60-bar window range on index names is **1.064%** (p10 0.555%)
against a median tick floor of 0.060% — room is roughly 18× the floor, and only
0.5% of #15's signals are *unreachable* even at the frozen 0.15% (the window
does not contain enough movement to pay). These families therefore do not fail
for want of movement; they fail because the measured entry-to-close return is
zero. Conversely, at the 1-minute level 83% of index minutes and 63% of mover
minutes have a range below 0.15% — a cost-based argument against
one-minute-horizon scalping, independent of any signal.

### 5. The exit dominates the entry — and #20 is the campaign that tests it

Within the *same* frozen entry set and the *same* 60-bar window, the span
between the as-measured exit and a perfect-foresight exit is **~69bp** for #15
(−0.041% → +0.645%) and **~63bp** for #19's long-direction events (−0.044% →
+0.588%). The entry contributes ≈0; the exit choice spans ~60bp. The foresight
column is an *upper bound* (no rule captures it), so this is not a promise —
but the direction of the leverage is unambiguous, and it agrees with the
daily-track finding of #17 ("the exits are well-timed; the system isn't").

**#20 (intraday exits) is the one unmeasured frozen campaign**, pending only
its 2,000-event floor (~2026-10-02). This screen raises its priority: it is the
only frozen campaign aimed at the ~60bp the entry does not own.

### 6. What this does to the quotes-data decision

- It does **not** rescue the timing families: the longs are negative before
  cost, and the shorts sit below the tick floor. A quotes feed cannot create
  4bp of edge into a 6bp floor.
- It **is** required for the mover population — but for the *cost model* and
  the #33 population question (does the room survive a realistic spread on $2–7
  names?), not to salvage his timing rules. If a data budget is spent at all,
  the mover roster is where it belongs.
- The cheapest useful next screen needs no purchase: run this same bound
  analysis on the **mover archive's** event set (restricted to the #33 roster
  population) with its own tick floors, and see whether mover signals have any
  room at all after two ticks plus a plausible spread.

### 7. Caveats

- The tick floor is a **lower bound**: real round trip = 2 × (half-spread ≥ 1
  tick) + slippage + impact + fees (+ locate for shorts). Nothing here
  estimates the actual spread, and on the mover population that unmeasured term
  is the dominant unknown.
- The mover tick-floor table uses the screener's session price from the three
  captured rosters (307 names, 400 name-days) — a small, recent sample of a
  population that turns over nightly, not its long-run distribution.
- The perfect-foresight and best-exit columns are **upper bounds** by
  construction: they bound what is possible, they do not forecast, and no
  pre-registered rule may be derived from them after the fact.
- S4 event counts exceed the archived families' n (2,401 vs 1,963 for #15;
  52,793 long-direction and 50,937 short-direction events vs 43,722 / 41,985
  archived) because this re-run covers 24 window bar-dates rather than the 21
  that existed at measurement time, and the archived families pair each
  direction against its own baselines. The two agree in sign and magnitude.
- This screen produces **no verdicts** and changes none. It is arithmetic about
  costs, and every number above is a bound or a mean of recorded bars — the
  tradeable-price question remains exactly as unmeasured as #23 left it.
